claims.text: Introducing a high density of hierarchical intragranular nanoprecipitates into a eutectic high-entropy alloy can simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
The target eutectic high-entropy alloy has a lamellar microstructure.
Hierarchical intragranular nanoprecipitates can be introduced as a precipitation-strengthening intervention.
Hierarchical intragranular nanoprecipitates are the structural mediator of the proposed property changes.
The nanoprecipitates increase strength through precipitation strengthening.
Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass of fine precipitates contribute to strengthening in a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The proposed precipitation mechanism also causes an increase in ductility.
The intervention is expected to produce an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 2.52 GPa in a eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is expected to produce approximately 5.2% failure strain.
Relative to conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys without nanoprecipitates, the intervention will increase both strength and ductility.
The expected response applies under room-temperature, quasi-static tensile loading.
The hypothesis is limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys having suitable compositions and microstructures.
The relationship among nanoprecipitate size, distribution, alloy composition, and strength-ductility synergy is not fully understood.
A controlled quasi-static tensile comparison of otherwise comparable alloys with and without hierarchical intragranular nanoprecipitates can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a significant increase in both strength and ductility would falsify the hypothesis.
